title: Working Abbreviations
body:
## Complaints and history

| Abbrev | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `c/o` | Complains of |
| `HPI` | History of present illness |
| `Hx` / `PMH` / `PSH` / `FHx` | History / past medical / past surgical / family history |
| `ROS` | Review of systems |
| `SOB` | Shortness of breath |
| `DOE` | Dyspnea on exertion |
| `CP` | Chest pain |
| `N/V/D` | Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea |
| `HA` | Headache |
| `AMS` | Altered mental status |
| `LOC` | Loss of consciousness (or level of consciousness — spell it out) |
| `F/C` | Fever and chills |
| `BM` | Bowel movement |
| `LMP` | Last menstrual period |
| `LKW` | Last known well |
| `ETOH` | Alcohol |
| `NKDA` | No known drug allergies |
| `WNL` | Within normal limits |
| `NAD` | No acute distress |
| `s/p` | Status post (after) |
| `GSW` | Gunshot wound |
| `MVC` | Motor vehicle collision |
| `Sx` / `Dx` / `Tx` / `Rx` | Symptoms / diagnosis / treatment / prescription |

## Orders, routes and frequencies

| Abbrev | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PO` | By mouth |
| `PR` | Per rectum |
| `SL` | Sublingual |
| `IV` / `IM` / `IO` / `IN` | Intravenous / intramuscular / intraosseous / intranasal |
| `subcut` | Subcutaneous (write it out — `SQ` is discouraged) |
| `NPO` | Nothing by mouth |
| `PRN` | As needed |
| `BID` / `TID` / `QID` | Twice / three times / four times daily |
| `QHS` | At bedtime |
| `AC` / `PC` | Before meals / after meals |
| `q4h`, `q6h` | Every 4 hours, every 6 hours |
| `STAT` | Immediately |
| `gtt` | Drop, or an IV drip |
| `KVO` / `TKO` | Keep vein open / to keep open |
| `NS` / `LR` / `D5W` | Normal saline / lactated Ringer's / dextrose `5%` in water |
| `NC` / `NRB` | Nasal cannula / nonrebreather mask |
| `ETT` / `NGT` / `OGT` | Endotracheal / nasogastric / orogastric tube |
| `I&O` | Intake and output |
| `mcg` / `mEq` | Microgram / milliequivalent |
| `F/U` | Follow up |

## Diagnoses

| Abbrev | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ACS` | Acute coronary syndrome |
| `MI` / `STEMI` / `NSTEMI` | Myocardial infarction / ST-elevation MI / non-ST-elevation MI |
| `CAD` | Coronary artery disease |
| `CHF` | Congestive heart failure |
| `HTN` | Hypertension |
| `AF` / `afib` | Atrial fibrillation |
| `CVA` / `TIA` | Stroke / transient ischemic attack |
| `COPD` | Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease |
| `PE` / `DVT` | Pulmonary embolism / deep vein thrombosis |
| `CAP` | Community-acquired pneumonia |
| `ARDS` | Acute respiratory distress syndrome |
| `DM` / `DKA` / `HHS` | Diabetes mellitus / diabetic ketoacidosis / hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state |
| `AKI` / `CKD` / `ESRD` | Acute kidney injury / chronic kidney disease / end-stage renal disease |
| `GIB` | Gastrointestinal bleed |
| `SBO` | Small bowel obstruction |
| `UTI` / `URI` | Urinary tract infection / upper respiratory infection |
| `TBI` | Traumatic brain injury |
| `SIRS` | Systemic inflammatory response syndrome |
| `OD` | Overdose |
| `Sz` | Seizure |
| `CA` | Cancer (carcinoma) |

## Places and people

| Abbrev | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ED` | Emergency department |
| `ICU` / `CCU` | Intensive care unit / coronary care unit |
| `OR` / `PACU` | Operating room / post-anesthesia care unit |
| `L&D` | Labor and delivery |
| `SNF` / `LTC` | Skilled nursing facility / long-term care |
| `EMS` | Emergency medical services |
| `BLS` / `ALS` | Basic / advanced life support |
| `MD` / `DO` | Physician |
| `PA` / `NP` | Physician assistant / nurse practitioner |
| `RN` / `RT` | Registered nurse / respiratory therapist |
| `PCP` | Primary care provider |

## Documentation

| Abbrev | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SOAP` | Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan |
| `PCR` | Patient care report |
| `EHR` / `EMR` | Electronic health / medical record |
| `VS` | Vital signs |
| `A&O x4` | Alert and oriented to person, place, time, event |
| `R/O` | Rule out |
| `DNR` / `DNI` | Do not resuscitate / do not intubate |
| `POLST` / `MOLST` | Medical orders for life-sustaining treatment |
| `AMA` | Against medical advice |
| `HIPAA` | The federal privacy and security law |
| `D/C` | Discharge **or** discontinue — always spell out which |

## Joint Commission Do-Not-Use list

| Do not use | Why | Write instead |
|---|---|---|
| `U`, `u` | Read as `0`, `4` or `cc` | `unit` |
| `IU` | Read as `IV` or `10` | `international unit` |
| `Q.D.`, `QD`, `qd` | Confused with `QOD`; the period reads as an `I` | `daily` |
| `Q.O.D.`, `QOD`, `qod` | Confused with `QD` | `every other day` |
| Trailing zero (`1.0 mg`) | The decimal point gets missed — a tenfold overdose | `1 mg` |
| Missing leading zero (`.5 mg`) | Same failure in the other direction | `0.5 mg` |
| `MS` | Could be morphine sulfate or magnesium sulfate | `morphine sulfate` |
| `MSO4`, `MgSO4` | Mistaken for each other | `morphine sulfate`, `magnesium sulfate` |

On the Joint Commission's watch list for possible future inclusion: `>` and `<` (read as `7`, `L`, or each other — write `greater than` and `less than`), abbreviated drug names, apothecary units, `@` (read as `2` — write `at`), `cc` (read as `u` — write `mL`), and the microgram symbol (read as `mg` — write `mcg`).

> **Trap:** The trailing-zero rule has one exception: a trailing zero is allowed when it reports a lab value, an imaging measurement, or a catheter or tube size, because the precision is the point. It is never allowed in a medication order.
